memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses said to the Lord, 'You have been telling me, "Lead these people," but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. You have said, "I know you by name and you have found favour with me." If you are pleased with me, teach me your ways so I may know you and continue to find favour with you. Remember that this nation is your people.'" - Exod 33:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses is carrying an impossible assignment, and he says so. "You have been telling me, 'Lead these people' — but you have not let me know whom you will send with me."

Notice he takes his frustration to God rather than nursing it in private. Honest prayer is not irreverence. God can handle our confusion far better than our pretending.

Then comes the heart of it: "teach me your ways so I may know you." Moses does not primarily ask for a strategy, a helper, or an easier road. He asks to know God. The way to survive a heavy calling, he understands, is not more information about the task but more knowledge of the One who gave it.

That is a prayer worth borrowing. We usually ask God to change our circumstances. Moses asks God to reveal Himself.

Paul prayed the same way — that he might know Christ (Phil 3:10) — and he prayed it for others, that God would give them the Spirit of wisdom and revelation so they would know Him better (Eph 1:17).

And see how Moses ends: "this nation is your people." He gently hands them back to God again. Whatever weight you carry — a family, a ministry, a workplace — it belongs to God before it belongs to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you bring your frustrations to God honestly, or bury them?
2. Do you ask more for changed circumstances or for knowledge of God?
3. What burden do you need to hand back to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me Your ways so that I may truly know You. This burden is Yours before it is mine. Amen.
